stats.label:
Yale Annual Endowment
Tax Bill Starting FY2026

keyDates.text: ED Secretary McMahon issues 'National Call to Action' letter to all university presidents and governing boards, requesting public statements on seven reform areas by year-end 2026.
Brown President Christina Paxson announces she will step down at the end of the 2026-27 academic year; national search for successor to begin.

Deadline for all postsecondary institutions to post 'statements of principle' on websites per ED Secretary McMahon's National Call to Action, covering admissions, free speech, AI, research integrity, and affordability.

All seven other Ivy League universities (plus 29 peers) file amicus brief in the First Circuit Court of Appeals supporting Harvard's challenge to the Trump administration's $2.2B federal grant freeze.
First payouts of ~$2,000-$2,500 per claimant begin in the $284M financial aid antitrust settlement affecting Brown, Columbia, Dartmouth, Duke, UChicago, Vanderbilt, Yale, and others.

OBBBA graduate loan changes take effect: Grad PLUS eliminated for new borrowers; graduate programs capped at $20,500/yr and $100,000 lifetime; professional programs at $50,000/yr and $200,000 lifetime.
New tiered endowment tax rates take effect under OBBBA: 8% for endowments above $2M per student (Harvard, Yale, Princeton, MIT, Stanford), 4% for $750K-$2M tier (Dartmouth, Penn, Vanderbilt).
Common App opens for Class of 2031 applicants. First cycle under full OBBBA loan environment; financial aid packaging at elite schools under heightened scrutiny.

charts.title: Estimated Annual Endowment Tax Bill by Institution (FY2026, AEI Estimates)
charts.footnote: AEI estimates based on IRS Form 990 filings and OBBBA tiered rate structure (8% for >$2M/student; 4% for $750K-$2M/student). Brown not listed by AEI as reaching 8% or 4% tier.

charts.title: Financial Aid Antitrust Settlement Amounts by School (Henry v. Brown, Settled Defendants)
charts.footnote: Figures reflect individual school settlement contributions to the $284M total fund. Cornell, Georgetown, MIT, Notre Dame, and Penn remain non-settling defendants. Vanderbilt settlement amount undisclosed. Payouts to ~200,000 claimants average $2,000-$2,500.

charts.title: Ivy League Federal Funding Received (FY2024, $M)
charts.footnote: Ivy League schools collectively received ~$6.4B in federal funding in FY2024. These figures illustrate scale of exposure to federal funding freezes and compliance pressure.

charts.title: International Graduate Enrollment Change, Spring 2026 vs. Spring 2025
charts.footnote: Data from National Student Clearinghouse Research Center. Declines are year-over-year for spring 2026 enrollment. Public 4-year colleges bore the steepest losses.
